issues.description: Field mismatch for Lecture.lectureName: the exercise UML and problem statement declare lectureName as type String (problem_statement.md, UML class attributes), but the reference solution declares a field of type LectureName (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10) and adds a LectureName class (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java). This difference in the declared attribute type (String vs LectureName) is not documented in the problem statement or template and will confuse students about which type they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field, constructor parameter, and getter/setter/toString to match the UML and problem statement (remove LectureName class); or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and template to introduce and document the LectureName wrapper type and adjust signatures/examples accordingly so students know to use LectureName.

issues.description: Constructor parameter signature mismatch for Lecture: the problem statement instructs students to implement a constructor that initializes attributes in the UML order with lectureName as a String followed by integer attributes (problem_statement.md lines 19-21). The reference solution defines the constructor with a first parameter of type LectureName (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 13-19). This causes a mismatch between the expected constructor signature (String, int, int, int, int) and the provided reference (LectureName, int, int, int, int).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature with the exercise specification. Either: (A) change the solution constructor to accept a String as the first parameter and store it in a String field; or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify LectureName as the first parameter type and show how students should construct/use a LectureName instance.

issues.description: Getter/setter signature vs field type conflict for lectureName in the reference solution: the solution declares the field as private LectureName lectureName (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 6) but defines public String getLectureName() (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 22) and public void setLectureName(String) (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 26). Returning/assigning String against a LectureName field is inconsistent and will not compile as written. The problem statement/UML expect lectureName to be a String (problem_statement.md lines 63-69), so this internal mismatch both breaks compilation and contradicts the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the type/signature mismatch so the reference compiles and matches the spec. Options: (A) change the field type to String and keep getLectureName()/setLectureName(String) as implemented; (B) change getLectureName() to return LectureName and setLectureName() to accept LectureName (and update the problem statement/UML to mention LectureName); or (C) keep get/set signatures using String but implement them to convert between String and LectureName (e.g., getter returns lectureName.toString(), setter wraps the String into a new LectureName) and document this behavior in the exercise if the wrapper type is intended.
